regions.Eastern Ozarks and Ste. Genevieve: French colonial Ste. Genevieve, then granite and springs: Elephant Rocks, Johnson's Shut-Ins, Onondaga Cave and a float on the Current River.
regions.Great River Road: The Mississippi bluffs between Nauvoo, Hannibal and Alton. Pair Elsah's stone village and Pere Marquette's lodge with Mark Twain's Hannibal across the river.
regions.Kansas City and northwest Missouri: The Nelson-Atkins and the WWI Museum, 18th and Vine for jazz and the Negro Leagues, Truman's Independence, and Disney's Marceline or St. Joseph on the way.
regions.Missouri River and central Missouri: Wine towns and river bluffs: Hermann, a stretch of the Katy Trail by bike, Benton's mural in the Jefferson City capitol, the Churchill Museum in Fulton and historic Arrow Rock.
regions.Southwest Missouri Ozarks: Ha Ha Tonka's castle ruins, the Wonders of Wildlife museum in Springfield, Laura Ingalls Wilder's farm and the Carver and Truman birthplaces.
regions.St. Louis Metro: Plan at least two days. Forest Park alone holds the free art and history museums; add the Gateway Arch, the Wainwright Building, the Pulitzer and the City Museum, and drive to Cahokia Mounds on the Illinois side.

sites.name: Gateway Arch National Park
sites.desc: Eero Saarinen's 630 foot stainless steel arch (1965), with a museum of westward expansion beneath it.

sites.name: Saint Louis Art Museum
sites.desc: Free museum in Cass Gilbert's Palace of Fine Arts from the 1904 World's Fair, with a David Chipperfield addition.

sites.name: City Museum
sites.desc: Bob Cassilly's climbable labyrinth of salvaged architecture inside a former shoe warehouse.

sites.name: Missouri Botanical Garden
sites.desc: Founded by Henry Shaw in 1859, with the geodesic Climatron and a large Japanese garden.

sites.name: Forest Park
sites.desc: The 1,300 acre park of the 1904 World's Fair, home to the art museum, zoo and history museum, all free.

sites.name: Missouri History Museum
sites.desc: Free history museum in Forest Park, in the 1913 Jefferson Memorial building.

sites.name: Wainwright Building
sites.desc: Adler and Sullivan's 1891 office building, a founding example of the skyscraper as a tall, unified form.

sites.name: Cathedral Basilica of Saint Louis
sites.desc: Home to one of the largest collections of mosaics in the world.

sites.name: Pulitzer Arts Foundation
sites.desc: Tadao Ando's concrete gallery (2001) with works by Richard Serra and Ellsworth Kelly. Free.

sites.name: Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis
sites.desc: Non-collecting contemporary art museum next to the Pulitzer, free.

sites.name: Mildred Lane Kemper Art Museum
sites.desc: Washington University's free art museum in a building by Fumihiko Maki.

sites.name: National Blues Museum
sites.desc: Interactive museum of the blues on Washington Avenue.

sites.name: Bellefontaine Cemetery
sites.desc: A rural cemetery and arboretum with Louis Sullivan's Wainwright Tomb.

sites.name: St. Louis Union Station
sites.desc: The 1894 Romanesque terminal with its Grand Hall, now a hotel with an aquarium and a wheel.

sites.name: Fabulous Fox Theatre
sites.desc: A 1929 movie palace in an exotic Siamese Byzantine style, with tours.

sites.name: Anheuser-Busch Brewery
sites.desc: The historic Soulard brewery with Clydesdale stables and brewery tours.

sites.name: Ted Drewes Frozen Custard
sites.desc: A Route 66 custard stand on Chippewa Street, famous for its concretes.

sites.name: Laumeier Sculpture Park
sites.desc: Large-scale outdoor sculpture across 105 acres in suburban St. Louis.

sites.name: Ulysses S. Grant National Historic Site
sites.desc: White Haven, the farm where Grant lived with Julia Dent's family before the war.
sites.wiki: Ulysses S. Grant National Historic Site

sites.name: Scott Joplin House
sites.desc: The flat where the King of Ragtime lived from 1901 to 1903.
sites.wiki: Scott Joplin House State Historic Site

sites.name: Historic Daniel Boone Home
sites.desc: The stone house in Defiance associated with Daniel Boone's last years.

sites.name: Mark Twain Boyhood Home and Museum
sites.desc: Samuel Clemens's childhood home in Hannibal, the model for St. Petersburg in Tom Sawyer.

sites.name: Mark Twain Cave
sites.desc: The cave in Tom Sawyer, a show cave since 1886.

sites.name: Hermann
sites.desc: A German river town founded in 1837 with brick houses and historic wineries.

sites.name: Katy Trail State Park
sites.desc: About 240 miles of rail trail along the Missouri River, with bluffs near Rocheport.

sites.name: Missouri State Capitol
sites.desc: The capitol in Jefferson City holds Thomas Hart Benton's mural A Social History of the State of Missouri (1936).

sites.name: National Churchill Museum
sites.desc: At Fulton, where Churchill gave the Iron Curtain speech, beneath a Christopher Wren church moved from London.

sites.name: Museum of Art and Archaeology
sites.desc: University of Missouri museum in Columbia with ancient, European and American collections.

sites.name: Rock Bridge Memorial State Park
sites.desc: A natural rock bridge, caves and a sinkhole trail just outside Columbia.

sites.name: Arrow Rock
sites.desc: A Santa Fe Trail village of 1820s and 1830s buildings, with a historic tavern and a summer theater.

sites.name: Ste. Genevieve National Historical Park
sites.desc: Rare French colonial vertical-log houses of the 18th century in Missouri's oldest town.

sites.name: Elephant Rocks State Park
sites.desc: Giant pink granite boulders lined up like a circus parade.

sites.name: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park
sites.desc: A natural water park where the Black River pours through chutes of volcanic rock.

sites.name: Onondaga Cave State Park
sites.desc: A show cave famous for its formations, near the Meramec River.

sites.name: Meramec Caverns
sites.desc: A show cave advertised on Route 66 barns for generations, with Jesse James legends.

sites.name: Ozark National Scenic Riverways
sites.desc: The first national park area created to protect a river system: the Current and Jacks Fork, with springs, caves and Alley Mill.

sites.name: Grand Gulf State Park
sites.desc: A collapsed cave system often called the Little Grand Canyon of the Ozarks.

sites.name: Ha Ha Tonka State Park
sites.desc: Castle ruins on a bluff above the Lake of the Ozarks, with sinkholes, a natural bridge and springs.

sites.name: Wonders of Wildlife
sites.desc: A large wildlife museum and aquarium next to the Bass Pro Shops flagship in Springfield.

sites.name: Laura Ingalls Wilder Historic Home and Museum
sites.desc: Rocky Ridge Farm in Mansfield, where Wilder wrote the Little House books.

sites.name: Silver Dollar City
sites.desc: An 1880s-themed theme park near Branson with Ozark crafts, music and coasters.

sites.name: George Washington Carver National Monument
sites.desc: The first national monument to an African American, at Carver's birthplace near Diamond.

sites.name: Harry S Truman Birthplace
sites.desc: The small Lamar house where Truman was born in 1884.
sites.wiki: Harry S Truman Birthplace State Historic Site

sites.name: Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
sites.desc: A free encyclopedic museum with Steven Holl's Bloch Building and Oldenburg's Shuttlecocks.

sites.name: National WWI Museum and Memorial
sites.desc: The national museum of the First World War beneath the 1926 Liberty Memorial tower.
sites.wiki: National World War I Museum and Memorial

sites.name: Negro Leagues Baseball Museum and 18th & Vine
sites.desc: Museum of Black professional baseball in the 18th and Vine jazz district, sharing a building with the American Jazz Museum.

sites.name: Kemper Museum of Contemporary Art
sites.desc: Free contemporary art museum near the Kansas City Art Institute.

sites.name: Arabia Steamboat Museum
sites.desc: Cargo of an 1856 steamboat excavated from a Kansas cornfield, perfectly preserved in mud.

sites.name: Kansas City Union Station
sites.desc: Jarvis Hunt's 1914 Beaux-Arts station with its Grand Hall, now a science center.

sites.name: Country Club Plaza
sites.desc: J. C. Nichols's 1920s Spanish-inspired shopping district, among the first designed for the car.

sites.name: Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts
sites.desc: Moshe Safdie's 2011 concert hall with a glass and steel shell facing downtown.
sites.wiki: Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts

sites.name: Thomas Hart Benton Home and Studio
sites.desc: The painter's house and studio, kept as he left it in 1975.
sites.wiki: Thomas Hart Benton Home and Studio State Historic Site

sites.name: Truman Library and Museum
sites.desc: Truman's presidential library in Independence.
sites.wiki: Harry S. Truman Presidential Library and Museum

sites.name: Harry S Truman National Historic Site
sites.desc: Truman's modest Independence home, kept as he and Bess left it.
sites.wiki: Harry S. Truman National Historic Site

sites.name: Walt Disney Hometown Museum
sites.desc: Marceline's museum of Disney's childhood in the town that inspired Main Street, U.S.A.

sites.name: Pony Express National Museum
sites.desc: In the St. Joseph stables where the Pony Express began in 1860.

sites.name: Glore Psychiatric Museum
sites.desc: History of psychiatric treatment in a former state hospital building in St. Joseph.
